one_line: Local-first training log where a coach agent and user share the same workout plan.
what_it_does: Creates, edits, and logs workouts through a browser-local fitness workspace with signed changes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central because the agent operates the same structured plan and signed state as the human rather than advising externally.
leverage_evidence: Pitch states the full feature set is exposed as 31 WebMCP tools.
Frames show chat, structured exercise cards, plan edits, and exercise logging in one shared workflow.
execution_rationale: The frame sequence shows a coherent end-to-end planning workflow with structured exercises, references, revision, and logging; exact tool outcomes are not always legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show agent working state and generated multi-exercise plan.
Frames show plan modification and later log-exercise interaction.
impact_rationale: Fitness users with equipment and injury constraints have a concrete need for plans that remain synchronized with actual training logs.
impact_evidence: Frames show knee-friendly three-day plan and workout details.
Product addresses the clipboard gap between coaching advice and tracking.
creativity_rationale: The signed shared human/agent training record and iterative plan-to-log loop are a fresh application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Every-change-signed concept is explicit in the packet.
Workflow combines planning, visual references, revision, and logging.
usability_note: Clear conversational workflow and editable exercise cards; dense states may require refinement.
advance_reason: High leverage with clear product motion and a credible complete workflow.

one_line: Browser-local FA(3) repair workbench with machine proof and human approval.
what_it_does: Selects an official invalid template, stages exact replacements, validates bytes/schema, and leaves approval in the UI.
leverage_rationale: Structured reads, exact replacement staging, and validation materially improve reliability over DOM-driven editing while preserving human gating.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies six page-scoped tools for workspace status, assets, exact replacements, and validation.
Frames show bounded proposal, requirement checks, and Schema valid state.
execution_rationale: The storyboard coherently progresses from inspection through requirement resolution and schema validation, though approval itself is only described.
execution_evidence: Frames show byte-locked source metric and highlighted inspected regions.
Final frames visibly reach Schema valid.
impact_rationale: Strict document repair has real value for teams handling regulated or format-sensitive submissions, even if niche.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies malformed FA(3) values as workflow blockers.
Human approval and proof are visibly emphasized.
creativity_rationale: The agent-proposes/system-proves/human-approves contract is a memorable, carefully bounded interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Product explicitly separates proposal, proof, and approval.
Frames show visible validation progression rather than opaque mutation.
usability_note: Auditable workflow is clear, but the technical dense interface is specialized.
standouts: Human approval remains separate from WebMCP
advance_reason: Strong safety-aware agent workflow with visible validation evidence.

one_line: Developer tool for explaining prompt-cache breaks and simulating savings.
what_it_does: Inspects LLM traces, identifies unstable cache prefixes, explains causes, and estimates split savings.
leverage_rationale: Domain tools can expose structured trace and cost reasoning more reliably than visual inspection, but the core analysis could otherwise be performed in a general tool.
leverage_evidence: Packet names list_traces, explain_cache_behavior, and estimate_split_savings.
Frames show trace/report-style UI states but no legible tool transcript.
execution_rationale: The frames show a plausible diagnostics interface and repeated analysis states, but text and end-to-end result details are thin.
execution_evidence: Frames show structured reports, tables, validation summaries, and visual analysis.
No clearly readable success/failure or agent result is visible.
impact_rationale: Prompt-cache waste is a concrete cost and performance problem for LLM developers, and the proposed explanations and simulations fit it directly.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets cache hit rate, stale tokens, and API cost.
Frames show analytical reports and visual summaries.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to interactive prompt-cache diagnosis is a fresh, focused developer-tool concept.
creativity_evidence: Combines trace explanation with counterfactual savings simulation.
Uses page-scoped domain capabilities rather than generic chat.
usability_note: Diagnostics appear structured, though small dense reports may challenge users.
red_flags: Agent invocation is not legible in the frame evidence.
advance_reason: Credible developer value and useful domain-specific tools, with moderate evidence limits.

one_line: Plain-language, agent-controlled live vocal effects chain with safety guardrails.
what_it_does: Lets a karaoke host browse or describe vocal sounds while an agent edits the shared effect chain with undo and protected limiter controls.
leverage_rationale: Natural-language intent is translated into multi-parameter audio-chain edits while human and agent share live state and safety boundaries; manual UI operation cannot match that translation as easily.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies ten tools for catalog, presets, chain inspection, and parameter edits.
Transcript documents agent preset loading, chain construction, undo, and limiter refusal.
execution_rationale: Frames and transcript show coherent simple/advanced views, chain changes, undo, and guardrail behavior; sonic quality is not assessable and does not affect the score.
execution_evidence: Frames show simple and advanced chain interfaces with changing nodes.
Transcript shows preset-first workflow, undo popup, and enforced terminal limiter.
impact_rationale: Karaoke hosts and nontechnical audio users have a clear desire to achieve vocal sounds without understanding signal-chain engineering.
impact_evidence: Plain-language vocal requests are demonstrated in the transcript.
Frames show accessible simple view alongside advanced controls.
creativity_rationale: A shared, audible, safety-constrained agent interaction model for live vocal processing is unusually memorable and well pursued.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent edit the same live chain.
Guardrails keep capture, bypass, and limiter decisions with the person.
usability_note: Simple view lowers the barrier; advanced routing remains available for experts.
red_flags: Sonic quality and musicality are not assessable from silent evidence.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP fit and visible guardrails; audio quality is appropriately excluded from scoring.

one_line: Overturn analyzes websites and generates a WebMCP retrofit plan and starter implementation.
what_it_does: Scans workflows, finds agent-readiness gaps, recommends typed tools, and generates code/report artifacts for conversion.
leverage_rationale: The product operationalizes the difficult design work of turning opaque site workflows into typed, human-gated agent capabilities.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes same-origin scanning, evidence-backed findings, tool inventory, and generated registerTool module.
Frames show Analyze/Find gaps/Recommend/Generate workflow and healthcare target UI.
execution_rationale: Frames show a coherent analysis-to-recommendation narrative and a concrete healthcare proof point, but generated artifact details are not legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show staged workflow and healthcare prior-authorization screens.
Frames show readiness metrics and recommendation/application sections.
impact_rationale: Website owners face a real adoption barrier, and the healthcare example targets consequential, high-friction workflows.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies prior authorization as a concrete workflow with large volume and appeal friction.
Frames show conversion concept applied to member services and prior authorization.
creativity_rationale: A product that retrofits arbitrary existing websites into agent-ready contracts is ambitious and distinct from a single-domain app.
creativity_evidence: One-shot analyze/recommend/convert framing.
Separates reads, proposals, and human-gated consequential actions.
usability_note: Staged workflow is understandable, though broad retrofit scope may make implementation complex.
advance_reason: High-impact infrastructure concept with coherent visible analysis and conversion flow.

one_line: A local collaborative room that turns unfinished observations into tested, credited learning.
what_it_does: Preserves sparks, adds perspectives and capability intentions, shapes honest tests, records learning, and prepares handoffs.
leverage_rationale: The agent joins and mutates the same credited local room state as the human, enabling structured collaborative sense-making beyond generic chat.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies ten imperative tools operating on shared state.
Frames show preserved contributor thought, observation form, focused question, and structured reality-check result.
execution_rationale: The storyboard presents a coherent thought-to-test-to-learning journey, but direct tool calls are not legible and the prototype is local-only.
execution_evidence: Frames show multiple workflow stages from spark through reality check.
Frames show structured outputs with risks, assumptions, and considerations.
impact_rationale: Groups doing reflection, research, or collaborative problem framing can benefit from retaining attribution and testing ideas rather than polishing them prematurely.
impact_evidence: Packet describes context, credit, sharing boundaries, persistence, and learning trail.
Frames visibly preserve original observation and contributor context.
creativity_rationale: The unfinished-observation-to-honest-test interaction model is highly original and pursued as a coherent social practice.
creativity_evidence: Frames emphasize keeping the person in the picture and sharing before certainty.
Reality-check and capability-intention concepts extend beyond ordinary chat.
usability_note: Calm document-like flow supports reflection; conceptual vocabulary may require onboarding.
red_flags: Prototype is device-local rather than live multi-user.
advance_reason: Distinctive interaction model and credible collaborative value despite limited direct tool evidence.

one_line: Chess game where a person and an AI agent share one validated board and take turns.
what_it_does: Exposes board state, legal moves, waiting, analysis, evaluation, and engine-strength controls as page tools.
leverage_rationale: Stateful turn-taking and structured legal-move outputs make the agent more reliable than scraping a changing board, though chess itself remains playable manually.
leverage_evidence: Packet lists eight board, move, wait, analysis, evaluation, and engine tools.
Frames show board progression, status/history changes, invalid-state highlighting, and later console inspection.
execution_rationale: Frames show initialization, many board state changes, feedback/error state, and debugging inspection; exact move sequence is not legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show pieces leaving starting squares and status updates.
Final frames show developer-console/tool inspection beneath the live board.
impact_rationale: Players and learners can benefit from shared play, coaching, and move evaluation; the audience is clear even if the domain is familiar.
impact_evidence: Packet describes coaching with Stockfish and evaluate-move capability.
Frames show a playable board and changing positions.
creativity_rationale: Human/agent turn-sharing with structured coaching is a fresh interaction layer on a known game.
creativity_evidence: Agent can pause for human turn and resume.
Advice output is structured to feed directly into make-move.
usability_note: Chess UI is familiar; shared-control and coaching states add complexity.
red_flags: Some exact move/error details are not legible in contact sheets.
standouts: Structured engine advice to legal move execution
advance_reason: Strong stateful WebMCP demonstration with clear game and coaching value.

one_line: Agent-native QA mission control linking requirements, tests, executions, defects, and release readiness.
what_it_does: Finds a coverage gap, creates and runs a concurrency test, diagnoses a defect, links evidence, and marks a release not ready.
leverage_rationale: The agent can traverse and mutate a linked QA evidence graph with structured actions, producing a traceable release decision that is difficult to reproduce reliably through UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes a 14-tool shared release workspace.
Frames show requirements, command center, readiness AT RISK, test cases, and WebMCP call sequence.
execution_rationale: The described central workflow is unusually complete and frames show the resulting linked QA states from gap to release decision.
execution_evidence: Frames show 100% passed yet AT RISK and 2/3 coverage framing.
Frames show command center, requirements, test cases, and explicit Release readiness AT RISK.
impact_rationale: Release managers and QA leaders have a concrete, consequential problem: passing tests can hide uncovered critical requirements and defects.
impact_evidence: Packet demonstrates missing critical coverage, negative inventory, defect creation, linkage, and not-ready reassessment.
Frames show release risk as an explicit product outcome.
creativity_rationale: The evidence-chain-first release workflow is a strong synthesis of agent actions and human QA governance.
creativity_evidence: Connects requirement, test, execution, defect, and release decision.
Frames include a dedicated WebMCP call-sequence explanation.
usability_note: Mission-control framing makes traceability visible, though the dense QA domain is specialized.
standouts: Correctly separates test pass rate from release readiness
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: complete, consequential, and deeply agent-integrated.

one_line: Question-driven climate dashboard that creates queryable visual answers from semantic datasets.
what_it_does: Answers climate questions with attributed data, charts, highlights, sonification, and alternate visual forms.
leverage_rationale: Page-native semantic tools let an agent compute exact, attributed answers and synchronize charts/highlights with the human view; screenshots or generic UI driving are materially weaker.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes 2,026 rows, four datasets, dynamic chart tool families, and exact attributed answers.
Frames show validated tables, time-series visualization, and blue-red climate heatmap outputs.
execution_rationale: Frames show a coherent progression from validated data tables to multiple visual analyses; audio sonification is not assessable but does not lower execution.
execution_evidence: Frames show repeated successful validation summaries and rendered charts/heatmaps.
Frames show table-to-visual workflow with no visible failure state.
impact_rationale: Climate learners, analysts, and users who need exact accessible evidence have a clear use case, including people for whom charts are difficult to access visually.
impact_evidence: Packet explicitly targets exact figures, provenance, and accessibility of chart data.
Frames show 2,026-row data report and visual summaries.
creativity_rationale: A dashboard that builds visual instruments from questions, including queryable forms and sonification, is an ambitious and memorable use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Packet describes chart creation, point highlighting, warming stripes, and century sonification.
Frames show multiple representations of the same climate evidence.
usability_note: Question-first interaction and semantic tables support accessibility; visual density remains a consideration.
red_flags: Audio/sonification quality is not assessable from silent evidence.
advance_reason: High leverage, impact, and creativity with strong visible analytical results.

one_line: Collaborative 3D room designer where agent layout proposals await human acceptance.
what_it_does: Lets people and agents place, move, measure, budget, and validate furniture layouts in the same room model.
leverage_rationale: The agent can use exact room geometry, collision checks, budget state, undo, and human-gated proposals; this is substantially more reliable than reasoning from photos or UI pixels.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies nineteen actions reaching the same functions and collision checks as manual controls.
Frames show 3D room variants, assistant/action history, and synchronized scene changes.
execution_rationale: Frames show a coherent conversational-to-3D iteration loop with multiple furniture arrangements and action states, though exact proposal acceptance text is small.
execution_evidence: Frames show room shell, furnished variants, layout changes, and sparse/reset-like state.
Right panel visibly accumulates assistant and action/result content.
impact_rationale: People planning real rooms need spatial fit, walkway clearance, door access, and budget checks that generic image-based advice cannot reliably provide.
impact_evidence: Packet lists measurement, budget, collision, and door-throughput actions.
Frames show actual 3D room and furniture arrangement changes.
creativity_rationale: Human-gated translucent layout proposals bound to live geometry are a distinctive and well-matched interaction model.
creativity_evidence: propose_layout waits for accept/reject in the page.
Frames show agent conversation paired with changing 3D scene state.
usability_note: Natural-language design plus familiar accept/reject control is approachable; 3D editing remains specialized.
advance_reason: Strong demonstration of WebMCP changing the reliability and safety of a spatial design workflow.
